text: The grant ID and the incident reference reach rwb-document as a signed, short-lived claim in the session envelope that gateway-bff forwards, with GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session of rwb-access as the authority behind it; the claim is read for the request and is never reused across a request, and a missing, unsigned or expired claim is treated as no grant, so the role's own letters decide the read and nothing is marked.
why: AC3 needs the grant and the incident on every entry written while the grant is active, and the legacy publisher does not exist across the service boundary; no source states how a consuming service receives them.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-039 section 4 step 7 and AC2; RWB-P4-E1039-CON 12.2 and 12.8; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-11 and DP-19
applied_in: RWB-P5-E1039-APP 3, 4 steps 2 and 4, 7 AC3, 8 BR4 to BR6, 12.2, 12.8 and 13
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-access owner and the gateway-bff route owner in the review of RWB-P4-E1039-CON.
impact: If the mechanism becomes a per-request call, one consumed row of 12.2, the fake of 12.8, the breaker of X8 and one build step change; no record field, operation or table changes.

text: An entry of a document content read carries capability area DOCUMENTS (the capability name of the API and of TSD P5 T6.1, in the upper-case form the legacy story uses for PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION), right R, the result value of a served read that the access contract defines, the case reference and the document reference of the version that was served, and no field ID, because the read returns a binary body and no field value; when the access contract publishes its code lists the service takes them from there and from LOV-DECISION.
why: AC1 needs an area, a right and a result to state the entry, and no source gives the area code, the result code or the field-list rule for a content read.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-039 AC1, AC9 and section 11; TSD P5 v2 T6.1 and API-P5-004; RWB-P4-E1039-CON 11
confirm: Data steward with the rwb-access contract owner before the record shape is frozen.
impact: If another area code or result vocabulary is agreed, one AC line, one row of section 11 and one fixture change; no operation, table or event changes.

text: This story owns the access entry of the document content read (API-P5-004) only; the metadata read of API-P5-003, the search of API-P5-009 with its DOCUMENT_SEARCH event of legacy RWB-E1-033 and the intake reads of API-P5-011 and API-P5-012 keep their own legacy keys and wire the same recorder when their stories are built, and none of them changes the shape of the record.
why: The legacy key names one document read and the technical specification names three more, so the slice needs a boundary that neither duplicates another key nor leaves a read unlogged without an owner.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-039 AC4; TSD P5 v2 API-P5-009 and API-P5-011 purposes; FSD P5 AC-ALT-P5-006-01
confirm: Solution architect with the P5 service owner and the owners of legacy RWB-E1-033 and the intake key.
impact: If more reads are ruled into this key, one AC, one row of 12.1 and two test cases are added; no table or event changes.

text: The incident of a read that cannot be recorded goes to the platform administrator queue named by a parameter row of this service behind the parameters contract of rwb-case, and the session answer that carries the grant is reused within one request only; both values are read as parameters and never written in code.
why: AC2 and X1 raise an incident to a queue the sources do not name, and the cost of the session read depends on a reuse bound no source gives.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-039 AC7 and X1; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-06 and the parameters default ruling
confirm: DevOps team with the platform observability owner and the P3 parameters owner before the story's Done.
impact: Two property values and one fake row change; no record field, operation or table changes.
